In India, the government has initiated a health sector reform program which includes revising and implementing new public health standards known as Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS). The IPHS aims to improve healthcare services and address issues related to working conditions in the health sector, especially for auxiliary nurse midwives (ANMs) who are a critical part of the healthcare system.

Under the Indian Public Health Standards, specific guidelines have been outlined to improve working conditions for auxiliary nurse midwives (ANMs). These guidelines include provisions for safe and hygienic work environments, sufficient staffing, proper training and education, and access to necessary equipment and resources.

In the context of health policy in India, there is a recognition that human resource (HR) management practices are critical for improving healthcare services and addressing workforce issues. As part of this effort, HR policies have been developed to address recruitment, training, retention, and career development for ANMs and other healthcare workers.

The relationship between human resource (HR) management practices and health policy in India is significant. HR policies are essential components of broader health sector reform initiatives, aimed at improving healthcare delivery, reducing healthcare disparities, and promoting universal access to quality healthcare services.
